title: triteleia ixioides subsp. scabra
intro: Triteleia ixioides subsp. scabra, commonly known as the Rough Bells, is a perennial wildflower native to the southwestern United States. This plant is traditionally used to treat various health issues, such as respiratory problems, fever, and skin conditions, due to its potential health benefits. The therapeutic actions of Triteleia ixioides subsp. scabra include its antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, and antiviral properties, which may help alleviate symptoms of infections and injuries. The bioactive constituents of this plant include isopropylamides, sesquiterpenoids, and phenolic acids, which contribute to its medicinal properties.
